name: St. Paul’s Cathedral
kicker: Christopher Wren’s London cathedral · Dome survived the WWII Blitz
briefing: After the Great Fire of London destroyed the medieval St. Paul’s in 1666, architect Christopher Wren spent over three decades building a new cathedral topped with a massive dome. On a smoky night in 1940, a famous photograph showed that dome still standing above the flames of the Blitz, and it became a symbol of British defiance. Winston Churchill ordered that the cathedral be saved at all costs.

tossups.p: Lightning destroyed the medieval spire that once topped the structure that stood on this site, and the Great Fire of London gutted the old cathedral in 1666. While designing its replacement, Sir Christopher Wren drew on François Mansart’s Val-de-Grâce church in Paris, which he saw on a 1665 visit, and on Michelangelo’s dome in Rome.
tossups.r: A hidden brick cone inside its dome belongs to a design that quietly departed from the shallow, spire-topped plan approved by a 1675 royal warrant. For 10 points, name this London cathedral whose dome famously survived the Blitz.

tossups.p: A tax on coal brought into the city helped pay for this building’s construction, which began in 1675 on the ashes of a medieval Gothic predecessor destroyed nine years earlier. Wren kept revising his plans even after ground was broken, quietly swapping in a taller, triple-shelled dome for the flatter design his original warrant had approved.
tossups.r: In 1723, Wren became the first person entombed in its crypt, buried beneath a Latin epitaph telling visitors who seek his monument to simply look around them. For 10 points, name this Wren-designed cathedral on Ludgate Hill.

tossups.p: This building’s dome hides a brick cone between two shells, secretly bearing the weight of the heavy stone lantern on top. Thanksgiving services for the Acts of Union and for the Treaty of Versailles were both held in this building.
tossups.r: Peace services marking VE Day and VJ Day were also held here in 1945. For 10 points, name this London cathedral whose dome famously survived the Blitz.

tossups.p: Workers paved this building’s floor with black and white marble squares, and its architect abandoned the shallow, spire-topped design in its original royal warrant. Part of its construction was paid for by a tax on coal entering the capital.
tossups.r: Consecrated in 1697 and declared finished by Parliament in 1711, this building took Christopher Wren about three decades to complete. For 10 points, name this English Baroque cathedral whose dome survived the Blitz.

tossups.p: A 1940 photograph by Herbert Mason shows this building’s dome rising above thick smoke during a night of German bombing nicknamed the “Second Great Fire of London.” Winston Churchill ordered firefighters to protect this building at all costs that night, even as bombs fell nearby.
tossups.r: Its dome, built in the English Baroque style, draws on both Michelangelo’s dome in Rome and the oculus of the Pantheon. For 10 points, name this London cathedral designed by Christopher Wren.

tossups.p: Climbing more than 250 steps inside this building’s dome leads to a gallery 99 feet above the floor, where a whisper against one wall can be heard clearly on the opposite side. This building replaced a medieval cathedral whose tall spire had been destroyed by lightning back in 1561.
tossups.r: That medieval predecessor was finally gutted by the Great Fire of London in 1666. For 10 points, name this cathedral that architect Christopher Wren rebuilt on Ludgate Hill.

tossups.p: Admiral Horatio Nelson and the Duke of Wellington are both entombed in the crypt of this building, which also once hosted a thanksgiving service for Queen Victoria’s Diamond Jubilee in 1897. Its architect is buried there too, beneath a Latin epitaph urging visitors who seek his monument to simply look around.
tossups.r: That architect, Christopher Wren, designed this cathedral’s massive dome after the Great Fire of London destroyed its medieval predecessor. For 10 points, name this London cathedral whose dome survived the WWII Blitz.

tossups.p: Sir Christopher Wren modeled part of this building’s dome on a Parisian church by François Mansart, blending it with ideas borrowed from Michelangelo and ancient Rome’s Pantheon. Construction on this cathedral began in 1675 and was declared complete by Parliament in 1711.
tossups.r: A famous 1940 photograph shows its dome standing above the smoke of the Blitz. For 10 points, name this cathedral on Ludgate Hill in the City of London, seat of the Bishop of London.

tossups.p: Prince Charles married Lady Diana Spencer inside this building in 1981, a ceremony held here rather than at the usual royal venue because of this building’s larger size. Decades later, Margaret Thatcher’s funeral was held here too, in 2013.
tossups.r: Earlier state funerals held in this cathedral honored Admiral Nelson, the Duke of Wellington, and Winston Churchill. For 10 points, name this London cathedral, the masterpiece of architect Christopher Wren.

tossups.p: This cathedral’s Whispering Gallery lets visitors hear a quiet voice carry all the way around its dome, 99 feet above the floor. Below ground, its crypt holds the tombs of Admiral Nelson, the Duke of Wellington, and the architect who designed the building itself.
tossups.r: That architect, Sir Christopher Wren, built this cathedral after the Great Fire of London destroyed its medieval predecessor. For 10 points, name this cathedral whose dome famously survived the WWII Blitz.

tossups.p: Winston Churchill’s own state funeral was held in this building in 1965, decades after a famous wartime photograph showed its dome rising above the smoke of the Blitz. English Baroque details cover its exterior, blending Italian and French influences with English cathedral tradition.
tossups.r: Architect Christopher Wren designed this building after the Great Fire of London destroyed the medieval cathedral that stood here before. For 10 points, name this London cathedral on Ludgate Hill.

tossups.p: A royal wedding between Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer took place in this building in 1981, and its massive dome rises 365 feet to the cross on top. Peace services for VE Day and VJ Day were held inside it in 1945.
tossups.r: Christopher Wren designed this cathedral after the Great Fire of London destroyed its medieval predecessor in 1666. For 10 points, name this London cathedral whose dome survived the Blitz.

tossups.p: This building stands on Ludgate Hill as the seat of the Bishop of London, rebuilt after fire destroyed the medieval cathedral that previously stood there. Its Whispering Gallery lets a whisper travel all the way around the base of its famous dome.
tossups.r: Sir Christopher Wren designed this cathedral’s dome, which miraculously survived German bombing during the Blitz. For 10 points, name this famous London cathedral.

tossups.p: Admiral Nelson, the Duke of Wellington, and the building’s own architect are all buried in the crypt of this cathedral. A famous 1940 photograph of this building’s dome rising above smoke became a symbol of British resolve during the Blitz.
tossups.r: Christopher Wren designed this cathedral after the Great Fire of London destroyed the medieval building that stood here before. For 10 points, name this London cathedral on Ludgate Hill.

tossups.p: The Great Fire of London destroyed the medieval cathedral that once stood on this site, so Christopher Wren designed a new Baroque building with a massive dome to replace it. That dome survived German bombing during the Blitz, inspiring a famous 1940 photograph.
tossups.r: Prince Charles married Lady Diana Spencer inside this building in 1981. For 10 points, name this cathedral on Ludgate Hill in the City of London.

trap.title: Westminster Abbey or St. Paul’s?
trap.body: London has two famous churches tangled up in royal history, and a clue about either one can sound similar at first. Westminster Abbey hosts coronations, most royal weddings, and the tombs of many monarchs. St. Paul’s is the domed cathedral you see in Blitz photos, and it hosted the unusual 1981 wedding of Charles and Diana along with ceremonial and state funerals for Nelson, Wellington, Churchill, and Thatcher.
trap.fix: A coronation, Poets’ Corner, or “where English monarchs are crowned” means Westminster Abbey. A dome, Christopher Wren, the Blitz, or a funeral for a military hero or prime minister means St. Paul’s.
